messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: standard errors cannot be computed as GroupPars.MEAN_1 is released
parts:
On second look, this actually seems fine to me and is really just a consequence of including non-linear constraints. The hessian is looking at the full parameter space and computed that way, which is not identified, while the model itself imposed a nonlinear restriction to actually estimate it. So the information matrix from solve(extract.mirt(mod, 'vcov')) needs to be fixed to include information about this constraint so that it's full rank. Seems pretty complicated if you ask me, but maybe there's an easier approach that I'm not quite seeing.

Phil

messages.subject: Re: standard errors cannot be computed as GroupPars.MEAN_1 is released
parts:
Hi Phil,

Perhaps you could try to fix GroupPars.MEAN_1 to zero by modifying two lines:

~~
pa = para[1:(length(para)-2)]          ----->  pa = para[1:(length(para)-1)]
sv2[c(ind,ind2),"est"] = TRUE        ------>  sv2[c(ind),"est"] = TRUE
~~

The SE could be computed in such case. So, that's why I suspected the inner code does not treat GroupPars.MEAN_1 well.

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: standard errors cannot be computed as GroupPars.MEAN_1 is released
parts:
Yes, the baseline model here is identified when the mean is constrained, but the standard errors are still not correct (they don't take into account the equality information in heq, so some may be to large/small). 

There are really only two solutions in my mind to fix this: 1) some transformation matrix is built up based on the heq() function so that pre-post multiplication of the unconstrained hessian is possible, or 2) don't use the EM, and instead adapt the BL method to compute this matrix numerically. The latter seems more feasible at the moment because conceptually the former is harder to obtain (there could be a trick that I'm not seeing though). Either way, I think for now I'll have to disable the SE computations when the alabama or Rsolnp algorithms are used.

Phil
